texts.li: Green light rippled over the sky tonight. {A_nameDef} stood out in the cold watching it, and noticed {X_indefinite} standing just as still at the edge of the field, head up.
Under the aurora the snow looked green, and so did {X_indefinite}, crossing the open ground in slow, unbothered steps while {A_nameDef} watched from the wall.
{A_nameDef} meant to go to bed, and stayed out under the moving lights until {X_indefinite} lost interest in watching {A_objective} and wandered off.
[child] {A_nameDef} lay on the cold ground looking up at the green sky, and {X_indefinite} came close enough to see what was so interesting.
In the middle of the day the light went wrong, and {X_indefinite} lay down in the field as if for the night. {A_nameDef} didn't blame it.
{A_nameDef} watched the sun go dark at noon, and saw {X_indefinite} at the tree line stop grazing and stand very still until the light came back.
[lowtech] Under the dark sun, {A_nameDef} heard {X_indefinite} call out from the trees, once, and then nothing until the light returned.
A star fell across the sky while {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} sat out by the gate. Among {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} said, you keep the wish to yourself or it spoils.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} counted three falling stars before {A_nameDef} saw one, and wouldn't say what {X_pronoun} had wished for.
[theirLowtech] A falling star, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, is a soul going home, and it's rude to point at it.
Under a bright moon, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the story {FACTION} tell about the face in it, which was nothing like the one {A_nameDef} grew up with.
{A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} sat up late by moonlight, swapping the names their peoples give the stars, and agreeing on almost none of them.
[theirLowtech] {FACTION} plant by the moon, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and laughed at the colony for planting by a calendar.
The evening stayed hot after dark, and lightning flickered silently along the horizon. {A_nameDef} sat out watching it, and so did {X_indefinite}, restless in the long grass.
Heat lightning lit the far hills with no thunder behind it. Out in the field {X_indefinite} lifted its head at every flash, and {A_nameDef}, on the step, counted them with it.

Fog came in after dark, and two eyes caught the lamplight at the edge of it. {A_nameDef} stood at the gate until {X_indefinite} stepped out of the gray, looked at {A_objective}, and stepped back into it.
{A_nameDef} heard {X_indefinite} long before seeing it, somewhere out in the night fog, moving slowly along the wall.
[lowtech] With the fog down, the torch at the gate lit nothing but itself, and {A_nameDef} only knew {X_indefinite} was there by its breathing.
The first frost of the year whitened the fields overnight. {A_nameDef} went out early and found {X_indefinite} leaving dark tracks across it, the only ones so far.
{A_nameDef}'s breath smoked in the first cold morning of the fall, and so did the breath of {X_indefinite}, out by the fence.
[child] {A_nameDef} ran out to crunch the first frost before anyone else could, and found {X_indefinite} had beaten {A_objective} to it.
The blizzard drove everything to shelter. When {A_nameDef} forced the door open to check the woodpile, {X_indefinite} was huddled in the lee of the wall, and {A_nameDef} left it there.
Through the blizzard {A_nameDef} could barely see the fence, but {X_indefinite} was there, pressed against the colony's wall out of the wind.

plain.li: [night] Green lights over the whole sky tonight. I stayed out far too long and I'd do it again.
The sun went out at midday, and the birds stopped singing. It came back. I'm still a little shaken.
[night] Saw a falling star with one of the travelers. I made a wish. Not writing it down.
[evening] Lightning on the horizon all evening, and not a sound with it.

warm.li: [night] Sat up under the moon with a traveler, trading stories about it. Theirs were better.
